sections.h2: What landlord tenant law means when you sell a rental
sections.html:
The lease, the deposit and the way a tenancy ends all travel with the house, so know where each stands before a buyer gets involved. Missouri has no single landlord-tenant code. The rules sit in Chapters 441, 534 and 535 of the Revised Statutes.

A rental that is sold keeps its tenant. The buyer steps into a house with a lease already running, a deposit already held and perhaps a month-to-month renter who can be given notice only in writing. The first piece of paperwork to plan for on a Missouri sale is a written notice to the tenants that ownership has passed to a new landlord.

An owner selling to a buyer who wants the property vacant has a different job. You cannot simply ask a tenant to leave on the closing date. The notice period, the type of tenancy and the court process all have to be respected, and the sections below walk through each.

A landlord may not demand or receive more than two months of rent as a security deposit. Under RSMo 535.300, the money must sit in an insured bank, credit union or similar depository, and any interest it earns belongs to the landlord. A deposit labeled as a pet deposit falls outside the statutory definition.

When the tenancy ends, the landlord has thirty days to do one of two things: return the full deposit, or mail the tenant an itemized written list of the damages withheld together with whatever balance remains. Mailing to the tenant's last known address counts as compliance. Before deducting anything, the landlord must give the tenant reasonable written notice of a move-out inspection time, and the tenant may attend.

The allowed deductions are narrow:

  • unpaid rent owed under the rental agreement;
  • restoring the unit to its starting condition, with ordinary wear and tear excluded;
  • carpet cleaning, only if the lease set that charge in advance and warned the tenant, with a receipt for the actual cost due within thirty days;
  • actual losses from a tenant who left without giving adequate notice, provided the landlord tried to limit those losses.

A landlord who wrongfully keeps any part of the deposit owes the tenant twice the amount withheld. Before you sell, settle the deposit ledger cleanly, ask your closing agent how the deposit will pass between you and the buyer, and put the answer in writing.

sections.h2: How a tenancy ends and how much notice is required
sections.html:
A tenancy with no written, signed lease is treated as month to month, and either side can end it with one month of written notice. RSMo 441.060 says the termination date must fall on a periodic rent-paying date at least one month after the notice is received. Oral notice from either party is not valid, and a lease running a year or longer must be written and signed.

A written lease ends on the date it names, and neither side owes the other notice unless the lease has an automatic renewal clause. A tenant who stays past the end date without a written agreement can be charged double rent. A tenant who sublets without the landlord's approval can also face double rent.

Three other rules can matter on a sale:

  • Mobile home lot tenancies shorter than a year need sixty days of landlord notice, counted from the date the next rent payment comes due.
  • An occupancy limit of two people per bedroom is presumed reasonable, though it does not apply to a child born to the tenants during the lease.
  • An active-duty service member may end a lease on 15 days' notice after a permanent change of station, certain long orders, discharge, or an order to government quarters, and is entitled to a full deposit refund if the other lease terms were met.

sections.h2: Removing a tenant takes a court order
sections.html:
A landlord may not evict a tenant without a court order. Grounds for starting a case include unpaid rent, property damage, a lease violation, staying past the end of the term, drug-related activity, illegal gambling and allowing a person the landlord previously excluded to live there. The tenant receives notice of the lawsuit and a chance to be heard before any removal.

After a judgment, RSMo 441.060 sets a self-help path with strict conditions. If the officer holding the writ has not delivered possession within seven days, the landlord has sixty days from the judgment to enter without breaching the peace, in the presence of a local law enforcement officer who has been shown the judgment and execution order and acknowledges that in writing. That acknowledgment must be filed with the court within five days after possession is taken.

Shutting off water, power or gas to push a tenant out is a different matter. A landlord who willfully interrupts utility service commits forcible entry unless the interruption is for health and safety reasons. If a rental is lost to foreclosure, RSMo 534.030 gives a residential occupant a notice from the new owner and at least ten business days before any possession suit can start.

Missouri tenants have very little room to withhold rent. In most circumstances a tenant has no right to hold back payment, and doing so can lead to eviction. The one narrow exception is repair and deduct under RSMo 441.234.

That section applies only to a tenant who has lived in the unit six consecutive months, has paid all rent and charges, and has not received an uncured written lease or house rule violation notice. The condition must hurt habitability, sanitation or security and violate a local housing or building code. The repair cost must be under $300 or half of the periodic rent, whichever is greater, and never more than one month's rent.

The tenant notifies the landlord, waits fourteen days, and then may have the work done and deduct the documented cost. If the landlord disputes the need in writing, the tenant needs a written certification from the local government that the code is violated before doing the work. Total deductions cannot exceed one month's rent in any twelve months, and a lease cannot waive these rights. If you plan to sell, clear any open repair request first, because a pending code issue gives a buyer's inspector something to cite.

sections.h2: Before you sell a Missouri rental
sections.html:
Start by pulling the signed lease, the deposit record and any written notices already sent to the tenant. Then match the end date of the tenancy against your target closing date. A month-to-month tenant who has not been given a proper written notice can stay, so a buyer who wants an empty house needs the notice served early enough to land on a rent-paying date.

  • Confirm whether the deposit sits in an insured account and what it totals.
  • Send the tenant written notice of the ownership change.
  • Close out any open repair request and keep the receipts.
  • Hold a move-out inspection only after giving the tenant reasonable written notice of the time.
  • Follow fair housing rules when talking with prospective buyers or tenants. Race, color, religion, sex, disability, familial status and national origin are protected, and the Missouri Human Rights Commission at 877-781-4236 takes complaints.

If the tenant will stay, a buyer who wants an investment rental may take the house with the lease in place. If the buyer wants it empty, the notice dates above set the pace, and a cash buyer who accepts the house as it stands can sometimes close without waiting for the tenant to leave.

faqs.q: Does a tenant's lease survive the sale of a Missouri rental house?
faqs.a: The lease stays in place unless it ends by its own terms or by proper notice. Missouri gives a seller no way to cancel a lease because a sale is coming. Plan on sending the tenants a written notice of the ownership change at or before closing.

faqs.q: What is the most a Missouri landlord can charge as a deposit?
faqs.a: Two months of rent is the ceiling under RSMo 535.300. Money a tenant pays specifically as a pet deposit is outside the statutory definition of a security deposit, so the cap and the thirty-day return clock apply to the general deposit.

faqs.q: Can I give a month-to-month tenant a verbal notice to move?
faqs.a: No. Oral notice from either party is not valid. A month-to-month tenancy ends only through a written notice that names a rent-paying date at least one month after the other side receives it.

faqs.q: Can I change the locks or cut the utilities to speed up a sale?
faqs.a: No. A landlord needs a court order to evict, and willfully interrupting water, electricity or gas is forcible entry unless done for health and safety. After a judgment, entry is allowed only under the conditions in RSMo 441.060, including a law enforcement officer's written acknowledgment.

faqs.q: Can a tenant deduct repair costs from rent?
faqs.a: Only in a narrow case. The tenant must have lived there six months, be current on rent, face a code-violating condition that affects habitability, sanitation or security, and give the landlord fourteen days after written notice. The deduction is capped by RSMo 441.234 at $300 or half of the periodic rent, whichever is greater, and never over one month's rent.
